ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, officers, authorised signatories, and beneficial owners of KR_YUHANGHOESA must be screened before incorporation and on a rolling basis against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the Consolidated United Nations Security Council Sanctions List, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit consolidated sanctions list, and the EU and UK global sanctions lists where relevant. The mandatory screening process must include a 12-month look-back for politically exposed persons, covering family members and close associates, using a commercial PEP database with fuzzy matching, negative news, and adverse media alerts. Every hit must be escalated to the AML compliance officer, risk-rated, and, if required, reported to KoFIU as a suspicious transaction report within seven days. Enhanced due diligence and senior management approval are mandatory for PEPs, sanctioned jurisdictions, or unexplained source-of-wealth events.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) at https://www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be written in Hangeul, and the suffix Yuhan Hoesa must appear at the end. The Korean registry applies a four-tier naming doctrine: (1) identical Hangeul characters; (2) identical pronunciation or Romanized transliteration as recognized by the Ministry of Culture; (3) deceptive similarity after removing particles, prepositions or punctuation; and (4) similarity of meaning or appearance, including English trade-name homonyms. A separate English trade name may be registered but cannot replace the mandatory Hangeul corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When a corporate name is rejected, the applicant must first file a written request for reconsideration with the Head of the Registration Section at the competent registry office within fourteen days of the rejection notice, grounding the request on the absence of identical or deceptively similar names in the cardinal index. If the registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may file an objection with the competent district court within fourteen days, and a further appeal to the high court if the district court dismisses the objection. The appeal must be accompanied by a copy of the rejection notice, the IROS name search certificate, and proof of standing to incorporate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Korean Commercial Act and National Tax Service practice require a physical business location for the registered head office. A P.O. box or virtual mailbox without a dedicated suite is categorically rejected for VAT registration and bank account opening. A full-service virtual office with a physical meeting room, door signage, and mail forwarding may be acceptable only for a registered-agent purpose, but banks in the Stripe/Paddle payout rail will still require a lease or service agreement and may conduct a visit. Home-office addresses are permitted only after NTS notification, but increased inspection risk remains.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist before accepting an address: (a) confirm the address appears on signage; (b) retain original board minutes and accounting records at the address; (c) have a responsible staff member available during business hours; (d) keep a signed virtual office agreement showing exclusive use of a suite; (e) display the business registration certificate. Quantified inspection risk: 15% within the first 24 months for a registered virtual office; 35% if the address shelters ten or more unrelated companies; and 5% for a standalone lease in a normal commercial building.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Republic of Korea Commercial Act, Act No. 1000, as amended, Articles 287-2 through 287-40 (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company), Article 172 (commencement, registration), Article 174 (creation of juridical person), Article 287-37 (directors and representation), and Article 287-29 (members meeting and management authority); cross-reference to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident subscribers
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Division, Civil Affairs Office, Seoul Central District Court (and its affiliated Registry Office having territorial jurisdiction over the principal office; also accessible through the Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration Office, I-REG)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa Formation Registration Application)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, the full amount of the subscribed contributions stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be paid or contributed in property before the formation registration is filed. The bank will place the paid-in capital in a blocked provisional incorporation escrow deposit account and issue a capital deposit certificate. Funds in this escrow account may not be withdrawn, disbursed, or pledged prior to the completion of incorporation registration, and the deposit certificate must be submitted to the registry as proof of payment. If incorporation is abandoned, the funds are released only to the persons who remitted them, after lawful cancellation of the formation process.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANGHOESA, A YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. THE FOLLOWING RESOLUTIONS were adopted at a duly convened first meeting of the directors of YUHANGHOESA (the Company) held on [date] at [time], at the Company registered office in Seoul, Republic of Korea, with all directors present in person or by teleconference and with quorum duly satisfied. WHEREAS the Company has been formed as a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act and has been registered in the Company Registry with registration number [registration number]; WHEREAS the registered capital and contributions have been fully subscribed and paid into the incorporation deposit account; WHEREAS the Company will conduct remote desktop access software, unattended machine telemetry, IoT monitoring, and digital consulting services; WHEREAS the directors are required to establish the initial governance, banking, office, and officer structure. NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The contributed capital is fixed at KRW 50,000,000, divided into 50,000 contributions of KRW 1,000 each. All contributions have been subscribed and paid in full by the members into the capital escrow account. The capital deposit certificate has been delivered to the registry. The directors are authorized to record the members in the register of members and to issue contribution ownership certificates when required. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company is adopted as [address in Seoul, Republic of Korea]. The Representative Director is instructed to maintain the corporate seal, minute book, member register, statutory books, and all records required by the Commercial Act at this address, and to file any future registered office change with the competent registry. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATIONS. The Company shall maintain a corporate operating account at a commercial bank approved under the Banking Act of Korea. The Representative Director is empowered to select the bank, sign account agreements, apply for corporate electronic certificates and security devices, open merchant settlement accounts for Stripe and Paddle payment rails, issue wire transfer instructions, and register online banking administrators. All payments exceeding KRW 10,000,000 require the additional approval of the Director of Technology or the Auditor as an internal control. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. [Name and passport number of individual] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] is appointed Director of Technology; and [Name] is appointed Auditor where required by the Articles of Incorporation. Each officer accepts this appointment and shall serve until the next annual members meeting or until a successor is lawfully appointed. The Representative Director is authorized as the sole legal representative before courts, tax offices, banks, regulators, and all governmental agencies. 5. GENERAL RATIFICATION AND INDEMNITY. All action taken by the incorporators to establish the Company is hereby ratified. Every officer is authorized to execute and deliver any agreements, tax filings, foreign exchange reports, bank forms, and regulatory submissions necessary to carry out this resolution. This resolution shall be placed in the corporate minute book and is binding on the Company, its members, and its successors. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned directors have executed this resolution on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign investment report confirmation and blocked capital deposit for non-resident subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA; designated receiving bank licensed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act; commercial bank branch acting as incorporation deposit account bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before remitting subscription funds, determine whether a Foreign Investment Report is required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. If any non-resident subscriber owns or will own ten percent or more of the issued contributions or will acquire management control through the subscription, file the Foreign Investment Report with the receiving bank or KOTRA and obtain the report acceptance confirmation. After the foreign investment report is accepted, open a provisional incorporation deposit account in the name of the entity to be formed or in the name of the incorporators, remit the full subscription amount from the investor's external account, and instruct the bank to mark the account as blocked for incorporation escrow. Obtain the capital deposit certificate in the Korean regulatory format, ensure the certificate states the depositor, amount, deposit date, and account purpose, and verify that no withdrawal is permitted until the formation registration has been completed. The deposit account must remain inaccessible to ordinary banking operations before registration. If the bank requires anti-money laundering documentation, provide the complete ownership, source-of-funds, and beneficial owner declarations immediately.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Report application form or KOTRA online submission receipt
Passport or national identity document of each non-resident subscriber
Certificate of incorporation, charter, or business license for any corporate subscriber
Articles of Association, member register, or ownership structure chart if the subscriber is a legal entity
Bank remittance instruction and source of funds certificate
Power of attorney for the Korean incorporation agent or resident representative
Beneficial owner declaration and anti-money laundering questionnaire of the bank
Provisional incorporation account application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or KOTRA queries, rejects, or suspends the foreign investment report, respond in writing with corrected corporate instruments, apostilled or notarized proof of legal existence, updated beneficial ownership information, and a revised remittance schedule. If the capital deposit certificate is withheld pending enhanced due diligence, provide an original bank reference letter and a source-of-wealth statement. If the report acceptance expires, file a fresh report and recompute the deposit certificate date before proceeding to notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, execution, and notarial authentication of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea; Korean Ministry of Justice notarial district office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, containing the corporate name, business purpose, principal office address, total contributed capital, value and number of contributions, names and contribution amounts of all members, methods of director appointment and removal, director term, auditor provisions, restriction on transfer of contributions, and the method of preparing notices. The business purpose clause must explicitly describe remote desktop access software, remote support tools, unattended computer monitoring, IoT telemetry, data processing, software licensing, and incidental consulting services. The Articles must be executed by every incorporating member before the notary. If a foreign member cannot appear in person, that member must execute an original notarized and apostilled power of attorney in favor of the Korean representative, and the notary will verify the agent authority and identity. For interpretation issues, provide a Korean professional translation accompanied by the translator certificate and a notarized confirmation that the translation corresponds to the executed original. The notary should issue the authenticated Articles as the final Chinese-free, Korean-law-compliant execution instrument.
required_dossiers: Original draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Member list showing subscribed contribution amounts
Passport and alien registration card or visa status certificate for each foreign member
Resident registration certificate for each Korean member
Certificate of corporate existence and power of attorney for any foreign corporate member
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney if the subscriber acts through agent
Foreign investment report acceptance certificate where applicable
Statement of contribution payment method and confirmation of escrow deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries a discrepancy between the Korean business purpose and the foreign investor registration, correct the purpose clause and refile a revised Articles page before the original set is authenticated. If a power of attorney is challenged for insufficient legalization, obtain an apostille from the issuance jurisdiction and provide a certified Korean translation. If the Articles of Incorporation are returned, re-execute the affected signature page before the same notary within the validity period of the power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation registration and corporate seal registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Registration Office, Civil Affairs Office, Seoul Central District Court; accessible through the Korean Supreme Court I-REG online registration system or in-person filing counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the authenticated Articles of Incorporation and the capital deposit certificate, prepare the Amalgamated Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company. Submit the application to the registry court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. The application must include confirmation that the paid-in contributions have been fully deposited, the register of members, the report concerning contribution payment, the consent writes for each director and auditor, and the certificate of non-foreign obstacles or the foreign investment report. The court will examine the legality of the formation, verify the registered office address, and issue a certificate of registered facts and assign a corporate registration number. After the registration is completed, register the corporate seal at the same registry office by submitting the seal imprint and the seal registration application, so the company obtains its seal registration certificate. File the application within the statutory filing window, which as a general matter requires registration no later than two weeks after completion of the capital contribution and notarization; the online I-REG filing should be made with the payment receipt attached.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company
Authenticated original Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
Register of members and contribution schedule
Report on payment of contribution or property transfer confirmation
Written acceptance letter and identity materials of each director and auditor
Corporate seal imprint form and seal registration application
Power of attorney for the Korean legal representative or registration agent
Foreign investment report acceptance certificate
Payment receipt for registration tax, education tax and court fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a preliminary rejection or suspended instruction, read the deficiency notice issued by the registrar and correct the specified provisions within the given cure period, pay any additional stamp tax, and resubmit through the I-REG portal. If the registrar questions the foreign investor report, submit the original KOTRA acceptance and a bank confirmation of the escrowed deposit. If the seal registration is rejected, correct the seal imprint format and reverify the identity of the officer presenting the seal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration business license, tax, payroll, and operational regulatory registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service HomeTax System; competent District Tax Office (including Seoul Gangnam District Tax Office where the registered office or business place is located); National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service; Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the certified corporate registration certificate and the corporate seal certificate, file the Business Commencement Return with the National Tax Service through HomeTax to obtain the company's Business Registration Certificate. The application must identify the principal business as computer programming and software development, ISIC 6201, and the registered office as the place of business. Complete the corporate taxpayer profile for corporate income tax, value-added tax, wage withholding tax, and electronic tax invoice issuance. Register for the electronic tax invoice system and obtain the digital certificate used for tax invoices. Open the fully operational corporate bank account with the business registration certificate, and connect that account to the selected payment rails, including Stripe and Paddle. If the company will hire employees, file the workplace establishment report with the Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service, register with the National Pension Service and National Health Insurance Service, and report new employees for each statutory social insurance scheme. After all registrations are completed, maintain the corporate seal, books, and tax records at the registered office and ensure that the first corporate tax filing and VAT filing dates are calendared.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration issued by the District Court
Corporate seal registration certificate
Business Commencement Return form completed through HomeTax
Articles of Incorporation and registered office lease agreement or owner consent document
Copy of Representative Director identity and passport
Original corporate bank account opening documents
Employment contract draft and employee resident registration data for insurance registrations
Foreign investor report accepted by KOTRA or the relevant bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the District Tax Office delays issuance of the business registration certificate, appear at the tax office with the original corporate registration certificate and the lease agreement, confirm the correct tax office jurisdiction, and ask for an immediate issuance receipt. If the online HomeTax registration fails because of mismatched foreign resident data, correct the foreign address and identification number in the corporate registration record, file a corrective certification request with the registry office, and then resubmit the business return. If payroll insurance registration is rejected, provide corrected employee hire dates and residence numbers and refile under the relevant insurance issuance portal.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation; relevant local environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - pure ISIC 6201 digital remote desktop access, screen sharing, and IoT telemetry software business with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, warehouse, or waste disposal facility
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emissions, stationary combustion sources, chemical storage, or hazardous waste generation arise from office-based software development and remote support operations; office electronic waste, if any, must be separated and disposed of by a licensed waste recycling company under the Waste Management Act and the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources should the company discard end-of-life hardware
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for civil defense fire permit because the business is non-manufacturing office software development and remote monitoring service. For the leased office space, the building owner must maintain a valid Fire Protection System Completion Certificate under the Fire Safety Installation Act and the local fire department must have inspected and approved the office finish. Before occupancy, the company shall obtain a change-of-use approval if the building occupancy classification is changed, and, when employees are hired, file the workplace establishment report with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act general duty of care, fire extinguisher installation, evacuation route marking, and first-aid preparedness.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); export customs clearance supervised by Korea Customs Service through the UNIPASS electronic system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A Yuhan Hoesa is incorporated in Korea; the court registration office issues a Corporate Registration Certificate. Step 2: The entity must file a Business Registration Application with the district tax office that has jurisdiction over its registered place of business, or submit the application online through HomeTax, within 20 days of the business start date. Step 3: The applicant must attach the articles of incorporation, Corporate Registration Certificate, proof of identity of the representative, lease agreement or other proof of a domestic business place, and a bank account record. Step 4: The NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number which operates as the VAT identification number and the corporate tax reference number. Step 5: A non-resident foreign entity that has no Korean place of business but is making taxable supplies in Korea must appoint a Korean tax representative and submit the tax representative appointment letter together with apostilled/certified copies of the foreign incorporation certificate, board resolution, and identification; the NTS will register the foreign entity under the non-resident business registration procedure and issue a registration number. Step 6: A foreign supplier of remote digital services to Korean consumers who has no domestic establishment may use the NTS special simplified registration for foreign electronic service suppliers through HomeTax, which is used exclusively for VAT filing and issuance of electronic tax invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic Korean corporation taxed on its worldwide income under the Corporate Income Tax Act, and is the VAT taxable person under the VAT Act. It is not a pass-through entity and cannot elect to flow income through to shareholders. Non-resident shareholders are not taxed on operating profits directly, but Korean withholding tax may apply to dividend distributions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Korean tax system does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election for Yuhan Hoesa. The only statutory elective relief relevant to indirect tax is the simplified VAT taxpayer regime available when gross revenue is below the statutory threshold, but that election does not change the entity's corporate classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean VAT Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No exemption threshold: every business operator must register with the National Tax Service from the date of business commencement regardless of turnover. For small businesses, the simplified taxpayer regime is available only when annual gross supply value is below KRW 80,000,000 (excluding VAT), but business registration remains mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue an electronic tax invoice for each supply to another business and transmit it to the NTS through the HomeTax electronic invoice system by the day after the supply. Transactions with final consumers must be documented through the NTS Cash Receipt System where the customer is a domestic consumer. There is no notarial real-time fiscal stamping; instead, the NTS enforces anti-fraud compliance through mandatory electronic tax invoice validation, automated cross-matching of invoices with VAT returns, and the mandatory use of HomeTax EDI/API interfaces by ERP and certified accounting software. Foreign non-resident electronic-service suppliers registered under the simplified procedure must file VAT returns electronically through the HomeTax non-resident portal and issue/download electronic tax invoices without any physical stamp or local fiscal device.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from South Korea and cleared through customs are zero-rated under the VAT Act. Services supplied to non-residents and consumed outside South Korea, including remote desktop access, online screen-sharing, SaaS, and IoT telemetry software, are zero-rated when the recipient is a non-resident, the place of service use is outside Korea, the supply is evidenced by a 0% electronic tax invoice, and the foreign currency proceeds are received or repatriated within the statutory foreign-exchange collection period. Inward payments in KRW from a non-resident are not automatically zero-rating; the taxpayer must prove the actual non-resident counterparty and offshore consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Declaration processed in the Korea Customs Service UNIPASS electronic clearance system)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or combined transport document evidencing physical exportation
Commercial Export Invoice and Packing List
Inward Remittance Certificate or documentary foreign exchange receipt evidence issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank

Executed service agreement/purchase order identifying the non-resident buyer and the exact remote screen-share and IoT software services; for pure digital services, platform service logs, IP addresses, and user telemetry may supplement or replace customs documents if the NTS accepts the service export substantiation package
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-match export declarations, shipping documents, electronic tax invoices, foreign exchange receipt records, and service audit logs. If the zero-rating documentation is missing, incomplete, forged, or inconsistent, the NTS will disallow zero-rating, reclassify the supply as a taxable domestic supply, and retroactively assess 10% VAT together with statutory additional tax for underreporting/unfaithful returns, delinquency interest, and possible input VAT clawback. Fraudulent export zero-rating or evasion of VAT may be referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, exposing responsible officers to imprisonment and fines, and customs authorities may also impose export clearance sanctions and revoke export benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank and monetary authority, acting in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Transaction Council under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a market-determined exchange rate system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account transactions are generally liberalized and require no prior approval; residents may freely receive and remit funds for trade, services, income, royalties, and current transfers. The Korean won is highly convertible for commercial bank transactions at market rates, and there is no mandatory surrender requirement for export proceeds. Capital account transactions, including inward foreign direct investment, portfolio investment, intercompany loans, and derivative exposures, are liberalized but subject to notification, registration, or reporting to a designated foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance. This registration structure is not a convertibility barrier, but it imposes real-time compliance documentation and beneficial-ownership verification. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are permitted after corporate income tax and withholding tax are settled; in practice the foreign investor must present a certificate of foreign investment registration or the bank's foreign-exchange purchase confirmation. For a remote desktop and IoT software company operating under ISIC 6201, recurring cross-border subscription receipts will be classified as current-account services revenue and may be received in foreign currency without restriction. Conversion into Korean won is immediately available through the foreign exchange bank at the prevailing market rate, with no quota, holding-period, or forced conversion framework. Overall, the KRW regime is best assessed as full current-account convertibility and high-but-controlled capital-account convertibility, with documentation and reporting discipline rather than government approval being the decisive liquidity constraint.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds and cross-border service-supply revenue must be collected and brought into Korea within six months from the date of export clearance or completion of the underlying service performance; an extension of up to two years may be approved by the Ministry of Economy and Finance for installment supply, open account contracts, dispute, or documented commercial reasons. There is no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; 0% of the foreign currency proceeds must be surrendered to the authorities. The registered exporter or service provider may retain 100% of the foreign currency in a designated foreign currency deposit account at a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank and may convert the balance into Korean won at any time.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Designated Foreign Currency Investment Deposit Account / Basic KRW Operating Account
Designated Foreign Currency Investment Deposit Account / Basic KRW Settlement Account
Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account / Won Operational Current Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account / Domestic Corporate Settlement Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account / Small and Medium Enterprise Won Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs and e-money institutions have low legal viability for serving as the Korean entity's primary treasury or settlement bank. They are not authorized under the Korean Banking Act to open domestic KRW current accounts or provide local bank sort codes. A non-bank payment service provider must hold an electronic financial business license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and must also be registered with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act to conduct cross-border money-transfer services. Foreign EMIs such as European e-money institutions or Singaporean major payment institutions rarely hold these Korean licenses, so their use is limited to offshore collection perimeter services. For the target payment rails, Stripe and Paddle may be used as offshore merchant acquirers and global payfac providers, but they are not bank rails in Korea. The Korean Yuhan Hoesa must instruct Stripe or Paddle to remit the net merchant payout by SWIFT MT103 into the company's own designated foreign currency deposit account at a Korean Tier-1 bank, with a clear service-revenue purpose code and a payout report matching the subscription transactions. Without the underlying merchant settlement report, the Korean bank will refer the receipt for enhanced due diligence. Recommended treasury architecture is therefore a licensed domestic FX bank as the sole primary account holder, with Stripe and Paddle used solely as off-balance-sheet collection gateways.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company, at least one authorized signatory, normally a director who is physically present in Korea, or a Seoul-based company secretary holding an appropriate power of attorney, must attend a Tier-1 Korean bank branch in person to complete the signature card, identity specimen verification, and AML interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by major Korean chartered banks for operational KRW current accounts, although a foreign non-resident director may open a strictly non-resident foreign currency deposit account under a notarized and apostilled power of attorney. The foreign beneficial owner with a controlling interest above 25% is not required to appear if the local authorized signatory performs the interview, but a certified passport copy, source of wealth file, and beneficial ownership register must be delivered to the bank in advance. The statutory directors are not all required to appear; a single locally resident authorized representative may execute the account opening documents, and the bank will then run the full corporate KYC on all directors and beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident founder and beneficial owner investing into a remote-support software company that has no physical Korean office at formation, causing an economic substance and source-of-funds underwriting red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized source-of-funds declaration; the beneficial owner's twelve-month bank statements from the remitting jurisdiction; audited or certified financial statements of the parent investor; a signed Korean business-address agreement such as a serviced office or virtual-office arrangement; the Yuhan Hoesa registered articles; a corporate organizational chart identifying the local compliance officer; and a fixed-asset or committed-expense forecast showing near-term Korean payroll and infrastructure costs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket cross-border merchant receipts collected through Stripe and Paddle from thousands of unlisted end users, which may be treated as an aggregation or marketplace-laundering pattern if the counterparties cannot be identified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The executed PSP merchant service agreements with Stripe and Paddle; last twelve months of mids and payout settlement statements; a reconciliation ledger matching every payout to a unique customer license key, remote-support session, or IoT telemetry contract; the end-user license agreement and privacy policy; a statement of software export services under ISIC 6201; and a live-database export or auditor's confirmation proving that merchant outflows equal application subscription activations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound paid-in capital wires from a related party or shareholder situated in a high-risk or enhanced-monitoring jurisdiction such as Hong Kong or a PRC financial center, triggering sanctions screening and unidentified-wealth review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A safeguards-screened corporate custody chain; the remitting shareholder's registry certificate and beneficial ownership breakdown; an apostilled or consularized corporate resolution for the investment; commercial database negative-news and sanctions-screening results; the shareholder's independent net-worth summary and bank proof; CRS and FATCA self-certifications for each individual owner; and the Korean foreign-investment notification receipt submitted to the designated bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export or service receipts outstanding beyond the statutory six-month FX settlement deadline because software subscription contracts are invoiced in arrears on net-60 or net-90 terms, creating a delayed-settlement compliance flag for the foreign exchange bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An aged receivables ledger with customer contract numbers; the master subscription agreements or online commerce covenants supporting net-60 or net-90 payment terms; Stripe and Paddle payout aging reports; board minutes approving the credit policy; a formal delayed-settlement declaration to the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the handling foreign exchange bank; and evidence that no tax exemption or export incentive has been revoked by the delayed collection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection for the Yuhan Hoesa must comply with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The foreign investor first files a foreign-investment report with a designated foreign exchange bank and receives an 'investment report certificate.' The bank opens a designated foreign currency investment deposit account in the name of the company or the investor, and the remitter wires the capital via SWIFT MT103 using a purpose code for acquisition of equity in a Korean company. The sender must include the foreign-investment notification number, the investor's full registered name, the Korean entity name, and the beneficiary account number. Upon receipt, the bank carries out interest and sanctions screening, confirms the source of funds, and issues a capital-contribution certificate or foreign-capital payment statement, which serves as the capital verification document for Korean tax and corporate registry filings. The funds may then be converted to Korean won at the market rate and transferred into the operating KRW account. For related-party capital contributions from high-risk jurisdictions, the bank will require the full evidentiary defense bundle before posting value.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements should be routed through the Korean entity's designated foreign exchange bank using fully documented settlements. For software royalties, licensing, and professional services to foreign suppliers, the standard clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 corporate-to-corporate wire with the appropriate services-payment purpose code and a remittance instruction referencing the underlying contract. For physical IoT hardware procurement, a commercial Documentary Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) is preferable for higher-value vendor contracts, with the beneficiary presenting commercial invoice, packing list, bills of lading or air waybills, and inspection certificates. For pilot equipment or recurring hardware purchases, Documentary Collections under D/P or D/A terms provide a lower-cost rail but require confirmed acceptance from the Korean buyer and clear unpaid-document handling clauses. All outbound KRW and foreign-currency debits must be supported by the master purchase agreement, vendor proforma invoice, Korean corporate tax invoice, title documents where applicable, and completed foreign-exchange justification forms; payout remittances received from Stripe and Paddle should enter as MT103 service-revenue collections and be reconciled to the merchant payout report before onward disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards in USD/KRW and EUR/KRW, available only with underlying actual or anticipated trade, service, or equity exposure, documented to the Korean bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act real-demand rule.

Foreign exchange swaps and FX swap points (USD/KRW) to cover timing mismatches between inbound subscription receipts and outbound supplier payments, provided the swap matches genuine cash-flow obligations.

Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps and interest-rate swaps for medium-term foreign-currency capital injections or long-term licensing arrangements, requiring bank approval and annual exposure reporting to the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for the onshore Korean corporate as a primary hedging instrument because the KRW is a deliverable currency and internal real-demand restrictions apply; any NDF transaction should be rejected by the treasury policy unless separately licensed and supported by a documented offshore presence requirement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Annual Financial Statements Tax Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea through the HomeTax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year; for any other fiscal year-end, on or before the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax for a completely omitted return and 10% of the under-declared corporate income tax for a filed but deficient return, plus a daily statutory overdue amount on the unpaid tax. Persistent non-filing and non-payment can result in compulsory collection, seizure of bank accounts and receivables, revocation of the business registration certificate after a final demand and cure period, and ultimately a court-ordered winding-up of the Yuhan Hoesa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Income Tax Surcharge Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax authority in the jurisdiction of the registered office or place of business, administered online through the WeTax local tax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than April 30 of the following year; for any other fiscal year-end, on or before the last day of the fourth month following the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or under-reporting of the local corporate income tax surcharge is subject to an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid local tax, together with a local tax overdue surcharge of up to 3% per month capped at 60 months. Delinquent local tax may be collected by compulsory attachment, imposition of a tax lien, suspension of tax clearance certificates, and refusal of registrations and public procurement licenses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return for the January 1 to June 30 VAT Period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing and payment due by July 25 of the same calendar year for each January-June tax period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the semi-annual VAT return attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid VAT, plus a daily statutory late-payment surcharge. Continued delinquency can lead to seizure of assets, revocation of the business registration certificate, assessment of VAT by administrative estimate, and criminal referral for willful tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return for the July 1 to December 31 VAT Period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing and payment due by January 25 of the following calendar year for each July-December tax period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the semi-annual VAT return attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid VAT, plus a daily statutory late-payment surcharge. Continued delinquency can trigger tax-induced business registration cancellation, mandatory field audits, and enforcement procedures including attachment of business assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax Aggregate Return and Withholding Certificates for Payroll, Interest, Dividend and Domestic-Source Payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual aggregate withholding tax return is due by March 10 of the year following the calendar year in which the income was paid; monthly withholding returns are due separately by the 10th day of the month following each payment month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold, file, or remit withholding tax may result in an additional tax of 10% of the unreported withholding amount plus a monthly non-payment surcharge. Persistent failure to file withholding returns can lead to a comprehensive corporate tax audit, penalties against responsible officers, and cancellation of business registration for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Independent Certified Public Accountant Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service of the Republic of Korea through the DART electronic disclosure system; National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea for attachment to the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Where the Yuhan Hoesa exceeds the mandatory audit thresholds, the audited financial statements and the independent auditor's report must be completed and approved no later than the annual members' meeting, with the audited statements included in the corporate income tax return due March 31 for a December 31 year-end. The DART filing is due within 30 days after the date of approval of the financial statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a certified auditor or to file the statutory audit report may result in penalties imposed by the Financial Services Commission under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Limited Liability Companies, administrative fines, denial of annual report acceptance, and mandatory correction demands. Sustained non-compliance may expose the managers to personal fines and provide grounds for revocation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Adoption of Annual Financial Statements and Profit Appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records maintained at the registered office; no public registry filing is required unless the company is a listed or designated public-interest company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual general meeting of members must be convened within three months after the close of each fiscal year, or within four months if extended by the articles of incorporation or by market practice for audited entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual general meeting does not create a government fee but may subject managing officers to commercial fines under the Korean Commercial Act, invalidate irregular dividend distributions, and create governance defects that obstruct confirmation of annual filings. No direct administrative strike-off attaches, but continued governance failure may be used by the tax authority as a compliance-risk trigger for a corporate tax audit.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Limited Liability Companies, an independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory for a Yuhan Hoesa if any one of the following quantitative triggers is met at the close of the preceding fiscal year: (a) total balance-sheet assets equal or exceed KRW 10 billion; (b) annual operating revenue, or turnover, equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion; or (c) the company employed an average of 1,000 or more full-time workers during the preceding fiscal year. Mandatory audit is also required if the company is designated by the Financial Services Commission as a public-interest company or operates in a regulated financial-sector activity such as banking, insurance, securities, or collective-investment services, regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS, the Korean International Financial Reporting Standards aligned with IFRS, is required for mandatory-audit companies designated as public-interest entities and for securities-listed entities. A non-public Yuhan Hoesa below the mandatory-audit thresholds may lawfully prepare financial statements under Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) or the Korean SME Accounting Standards, provided that the reported book income is reconciled to taxable income under the Corporate Income Tax Law for the corporate tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not operate a public beneficial-ownership register or impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing. Instead, the Yuhan Hoesa is required to maintain a complete and accurate register of members at the registered office and to record every transfer of membership units without delay. Each transfer of a membership interest must be evidenced by a members' resolution or managerial approval under the articles of incorporation, and the register must be amended before the new member may exercise voting or distribution rights. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, any acquisition, disposal, or material change in the membership interest of a non-resident shareholder or foreign-invested entity must be reported to the designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days from the closing date of the transaction. The statutory corporate income tax return schedules must also disclose the identities, tax residences, and shareholding ratios of all significant ultimate beneficial owners as part of the annual tax compliance record.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Encumbrances over Company Assets
Minute Book of Members' General Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $600 - $2,200 per year for a registered office and corporate secretarial agent service in Seoul or a regional business hub
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000 - $15,000 per year depending on transaction volume, group structure, intercompany balances, and whether K-GAAP or K-IFRS financial statements are required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% national corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax, producing a 29.7% combined top marginal effective headline rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act for foreign-invested technology businesses in Free Economic Zones; 30% to 50% corporate income tax reduction for up to 5 years in eligible Free Economic Zones; R&D and manpower development tax deduction of up to 50% of qualifying expenditures; technology transfer income exclusion for qualifying patents and software copyrights; temporary investment tax credits for digital infrastructure and ICT service platforms, including remote-connection and telemetry software

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return and Taxable Income Calculation Form (Form 57-1) filed electronically via the National Tax Service HomeTax system at hometax.go.kr; local income tax surcharge return is filed jointly with the same return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly preliminary corporate tax prepayments are required during the fiscal year for corporate taxpayers with taxable income in the immediately preceding year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final annual return due within three months after the end of the fiscal year (April 30 for a calendar-year taxpayer); a one-month extension is available upon filing an extension application with a provisional return and payment estimate; quarterly prepayments are due by the last day of the second month of each quarter

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identity and registration information: business registration number, legal entity name, corporate domicile, representative director name, tax classification, and fiscal year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean-domiciled Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident shareholders, identify the foreign shareholders' jurisdictions in the attached residence status schedule; designate a domestic representative for service of process; do not alter the fiscal year without prior approval because all filing deadlines and preliminary prepayment computations are measured from the fiscal year-end shown in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of comprehensive income by classification: gross revenue, sales, cost of sales, gross profit, selling, general and administrative expenses, operating income, non-operating income, non-operating expenses, and pre-tax book net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report remote desktop access and unattended machine telemetry software revenue gross in revenue; include cloud subscription fees, usage-based telemetry fees, device licensing fees and remote support fees; segregate export sales from domestic sales because the Korean export tax reduction and transfer pricing screening thresholds are computed using the revenue amounts in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation: book net income plus non-deductible expenses and tax-exempt income, minus income excluded from Korean corporate income tax and statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust intercompany royalties, management fees, and service fees paid to non-resident related parties; excessive or artificial payments lacking economic substance are disallowed under the Corporate Tax Act and local income tax surcharge is reassessed in proportion to the corrected taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward and tax base computation: current-year taxable income, net operating loss carryforward utilization, tax base exemption amount, and aggregation of domestic and foreign business establishment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is subject to tax on worldwide income; foreign permanent establishment losses may be limited, so include only deductible Korean-source net operating loss carryforwards; do not offset outbound dividend withholding tax or treaty-exempt foreign income in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National corporate income tax computation at progressive brackets, 10% local income tax surcharge, tax credits, tax reductions, foreign investment credit, and total final corporate tax and local tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the progressive national brackets: 9% on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income, 19% over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion, 24% over KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion, and 27% over KRW 300 billion; then add the 10% local income tax surcharge; the net effective rate ranges from 9.9% to 29.7%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income, foreign tax credit, controlled foreign corporation income, outbound dividend declarations, interest and royalty remittance withholding, and the bilateral tax treaty benefit schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all remittances to non-resident shareholders, including dividends, interest, royalties, lease charges and service fees; withhold the statutory foreign taxpayer tax in compliance with the payment date rules; attach the non-resident recipient's Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership statement, and the specific Double Taxation Agreement article relied upon; failure to attach a valid TRC before payment converts treaty relief into an assessment at the full 22% withholding rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction schedule and transfer pricing documentation index: cross-border sales, intercompany services, royalties, financing, margins, profits, and the transfer pricing method used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the transaction list with foreign related parties for every cross-border related-party payment, regardless of amount; the transfer pricing method selected must be documented; if the ability to claim application of the arm's length principle is not adequately evidenced, the tax authority will use its adjusted arm's length price authority and add a negligence penalty on the understated income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachment index for statutory schedules: financial statements, audit opinion if required, tax adjustment schedules, foreign account reporting, and economic substance explanations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the non-resident director minutes, substance records, employee payroll and insurance records, local office lease contracts, board resolutions approving dividends, and a copy of the Tax Residency Certificate file; these records prove that the Yuhan Hoesa is not a shell and that the beneficial owners are entitled to treaty protection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs an unfaithful penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax under Article 47-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; negligent under-reporting adds an additional 10% penalty under Article 47-3; unpaid tax accrues a daily delayed-payment surcharge while in arrears; fraudulent concealment of revenue or fabricated offshore expenses triggers the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to three times the tax evaded, or both; serious repeat evasion or evasion above statutory thresholds may additionally lead to public disclosure of the taxpayer and criminal indictment of the responsible director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on dividends paid to a non-resident corporate or individual shareholder, composed of 20% national withholding tax and 2% local income tax surcharge; bilateral treaty rates may reduce the tax to 5% to 15% depending on beneficial ownership, holding percentage, and the applicable Double Taxation Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The withholding agent must obtain and retain before remittance: the Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient is not a conduit or nominee, evidence of the shareholding percentage and minimum holding period required by the treaty, and a duly completed application for treaty tax reduction or exemption submitted through HomeTax or to the competent local tax office; the Korean payer must file the withholding return and remit the reduced tax within the statutory deadline after payment; failure to substantiate the recipient with a TRC and economic substance causes the treaty benefit to be denied and the full 22% statutory rate to be assessed, which may be appealed through the Mutual Agreement Procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalty and interest payments is 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge); under most Korean bilateral treaties the rate is reduced to approximately 5% to 10% for interest and 2% to 15% for royalties, subject to a valid TRC, beneficial ownership, and the absence of treaty-shopping abuse.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border related-party transaction value exceeding KRW 10 billion of aggregate annual intercompany transactions requires the integrated Local File and transfer pricing disclosure submitted with the corporate income tax return; a group-wide Master File is additionally required when the Korean entity is a member of a multinational group whose consolidated annual group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion; SMEs with aggregate cross-border related-party transactions below the statutory de minimis exemption thresholds remain required to maintain contemporaneous arm's length documentation for all intercompany transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply an offshore Economic Substance Regulations regime in the Caribbean sense, but the statutory substance-over-form principle, the General Anti-Abuse Rule under the Framework Act on National Taxes, the controlled foreign company rules, and the Korean domestic permanent establishment threshold in the Corporate Tax Act require a Yuhan Hoesa to execute its core income-generating activities in Korea; the entity must maintain a local office, board minutes, employees, service contracts, bank accounts, financial books, and an effective management presence; a Korean entity used merely as a treasury or intermediary for non-resident owners without capacity to perform its core remote-screen-share and telemetry functions will be recharacterized as a conduit, with treaty relief denied and outbound payments reclassified as taxable dividends or business income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Revenue Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa intentionally omits remote screen share subscription revenue collected through Stripe or Paddle from the corporate income tax return, or records such revenue in personal bank accounts of foreign directors, or fabricates deductible expenses through fake invoices for IT consultancy with an offshore shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1) attracts imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to three times the amount of tax evaded, or both; the tax authority also imposes the 20% unfaithful return penalty and a 10% negligent under-reporting penalty under Articles 47-2 and 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus refund of the evaded national corporate tax and the 10% local income tax surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director is jointly and severally liable with the corporation for unpaid tax, penalties, and delayed-payment surcharge to the extent of the corporate assets and can be made to contribute personal assets if tax was illegally concealed or misappropriated; the National Tax Service may impose a travel ban and blacklisting for tax arrears, and criminal conviction results in disqualification as a director and imprisonment up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Treaty Shopping Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa is formed with no real office, no employees, no actual management decision-making, and no business purpose other than making outbound dividend payments to foreign related parties at reduced treaty rates while the true core income-generating activities of remote software development, licensing, support, and IoT data processing are conducted by non-resident shareholders outside Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority recharacterizes the entity as a conduit under Article 171 of the Corporate Tax Act and Articles 6 and 11 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, denies the treaty withholding rate, and assesses the full 22% withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties; the entity is subject to a 20% unfaithful disclosure penalty and the restored corporate tax may be imposed on the deemed income allocated to the Korean enterprise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the sham structure are personally liable for the withheld shortfall and penalties, are exposed to the National Tax Service seizure of personal assets under the principle of real controlling taxpayer liability, face a Korean overseas travel restriction or exit ban if tax arrears are outstanding, and can be criminally prosecuted as accomplices in tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa executes large intercompany royalty, technical service, or remote-support fees to a non-resident parent without contemporaneous arm's length analysis, without a written contract, and without evidence that the foreign related party performs substantial functions or bears economic risk; the fees are simply used to shift Korean profits abroad and avoid Korean corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 5 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, the National Tax Service shall determine the appropriate arm's length price and adjust the Korean taxable income; the understated foreign-related transaction income triggers an additional adjustment penalty and the disallowed expense is treated as a constructive dividend or deemed contribution, with 22% withholding tax applied where the payment is actually a disguised dividend to a non-resident shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are responsible for filing inaccurate transfer pricing reports may be held civilly liable for resulting tax losses; if the false related-party transaction is found to be fraudulent and deliberate, the director faces the criminal tax evasion penalty of imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine of up to three times the evaded tax, as well as personal asset tracing, director disqualification, and listing by the National Tax Service as an habitual non-compliant taxpayer under the public disclosure system.
